_what: Bright Data's OWN telemetry about our collections, recorded where it disagrees with our health board.
_why_this_file_exists: Our health board computes `fails` from what the collector returned to us. That is self-reported health, and self-reported health cannot see a page that never reached us. On 2026-08-20 the platform's monitoring flagged a 20% page failure on a US collection while our own board recorded fails: 0 for the US arm on that day. Neither number is wrong. They measure different things, and the distance between them is a real limitation of every health board that only reads its own output. This project exists to refuse clean screens over broken scrapers, so the honest move is to publish both numbers and name the gap, not to quietly adopt theirs or ignore it.
_provenance: Transcribed from a Bright Data 'Low success rate' alert email, subject line "Low success rate for canon-us", received 2026-08-21. It is operator-supplied evidence, not an API read: we do not currently poll the platform for job telemetry, which is itself the finding. Nothing here is inferred and nothing is rounded.
_limitation: This is ONE job. It is not a success rate for the sweep, for the US arm, or for any other collection, and it must never be presented as one. Eight pages is a small run and 2 failures out of 8 carries an interval far too wide to characterise anything.

jobs.collector_id_note: The alert names the collector 'canon-us'. This project has run more than one US collector (c_mt01usw31e8y5ubqjs on the current sweep, c_mt1fh690ebsllah9n in heal US-002), and the alert does not carry an id. Mapping the name to an id would be a guess, so it is left null.
jobs.our_board_said: fails: 0 for the US arm in every health file written on 2026-08-20
jobs.reconciliation: Not a contradiction. Our `fails` counts inputs that returned neither a row nor an archived empty-result page, computed from collector output. The platform counts pages it could not collect. A page that failed at the fetch layer and returned nothing is a failure to them and simply an absent input to us. We could not have seen these two without being told.

jobs.collector_id_note: The alert names the collector 'canon-in' and carries no id. The IN arm on the published sweep is c_mt03cj5z2fo651wy8q; mapping the name to that id would be a guess, so it is left null.
jobs.job_id: six collections: j_mt2r6kugxdxhieg9t, j_mt2vevjsavi1er7s0, j_mt2z9ipf1fq0ockb8l, j_mt30p0cwr7lvj2kks, j_mt31833267s9ow7xa, j_mt33zfxy13ak58zo99
jobs.our_board_said: fails: 0 for the IN arm, which was not a measurement
jobs.reconciliation: The India collector degraded across 21 August, from 44% of pages failing on the first collection to 96% on the last. Our board reported fails: 0 for that arm on the same day. It was not wrong so much as not asking: collector/sweep.py set fails=0 on the replay path, and a replay re-scores rows already in the archive without issuing a request, so it cannot observe a fetch failure. Asserting 0 turned 'we did not look' into 'nothing went wrong'. That path now records fails as not-measured and the arm card says so.
jobs.does_this_affect_the_published_figures: No, and this was checked rather than assumed. data/sweeps/raw/IN.jsonl was captured 2026-08-20 at 21:06 UTC. Every one of the six failing collections began on 21 August, after it. No row from them reached the archive, the payload or the wall. What they do establish is that the collector is degraded NOW: anyone re-running the India arm today gets almost nothing back.
jobs.what_it_cost: 2,500 pages and 11,886 errors across six collections. The error count exceeds the page count because failed pages were retried. What that spent is on the account, not in the sweep output, and this project does not state a billing figure it cannot derive.

_result: Two alerts, and between them they make the same point twice. Bright Data's own monitoring saw a 20% page failure on a US collection and then a collapse to 17% success on the India collector, and on both days our health board reported zero fails for those arms. The board reads what the collector handed us; the platform reads what happened at the fetch layer. We only know because we were told.
